name: secret-list
title: Secret List
description: SecretList: stored secrets, like API keys, as rows with their name, a mask with the fingerprint the server supplies (•••• abcd), a configured or missing StatusPill, created, updated and last-used dates, and Replace and Delete. The data type has no value field. Loading, empty and error come through DataState. Agents can replace and delete by id; delete waits for a person.
docs:
`<SecretList aria-label="API keys" secrets={secrets} status={status} error={error} onRetry={refetch} onReplace={(id) => setReplacing(id)} onDelete={(id) => api.delete(id)} text={{ configured: "Configured", missing: "Missing", replace: "Replace", delete: "Delete", updated: (time) => <>Updated {time}</>, … }} />`.

A `StoredSecret` is `{ id, name, configured, fingerprint?, description?, createdAt?, updatedAt?, lastUsedAt? }` and has no value field: the list can't show a value because it never gets one. `fingerprint` is whatever few characters your server derives, like the last four, shown after a mask and read as "Hidden value ending in a1b2" (`labels.fingerprint`); a configured secret without one shows the mask alone, and a missing one no mask, a warning status and `text.set` on its replace button. `lastUsedAt: null` shows `text.neverUsed`. Dates are RelativeTimes, by `locale`.

Replace runs `onReplace(id)`: open a `FormDialog` with `<FormField name="value"><Input sensitive revealable /></FormField>`, which never puts the new value in the DOM and clears it once saved. Delete opens a ConfirmDialog whose confirm button carries `data-agent-confirm` (`text.deleteAgentConfirm`) and runs `onDelete(id)`, pending while its Promise runs. Agents read the secrets as the list's items, by id and name, and call `replace(id)` and `delete(id)`, which opens the confirmation, so the delete itself waits for a person; an unknown id, or an action without its callback, fails the step with why.

Rows are a List rather than a DataTable: a handful of secrets with two actions each read better as rows that stack on a phone than as columns, and each row's buttons are named for its secret. Every visible word comes from `text`; `labels` holds the screen-reader names, in English by default.

**Per secret.** Delete shows on configured secrets only (an agent's `delete` of a missing one fails with why). `deleteTitle`, `deleteDescription`, `deleteConfirm` and `deleteAgentConfirm` take a string or a function of the secret, to name it: `deleteTitle: (secret) => `Delete ${secret.name}?``. The button of a missing secret holds `text.set` (falling back to `text.replace`) and is named by `labels.setSecret(name)`, "Set GitHub token", so its name matches what it says.
